correctness.rationale: Exact count formula by total coin number t decomposes every representation uniquely. Proven one-way injection d(n+a)>=d(n) reduces global maximum to candidate and its a successors. Separate formulas for all 3 regimes and both parities show d(candidate)=p and successor counts >=p+1; all boundary values, incl p=0,a odd, and p=2a, are addressed. Independent integer DP confirms 14,632 (a,p) cases with a up to 120; a second combinatorial sum checks 3,374 n. These computations supplement, not replace, the general proof.

originality.rationale: Komatsu–Ying 2022 (arXiv:2206.13052) proves only p<=floor(a/2), and specifically poses the problem of formulas for larger p. The novel portion is the exact linear-window piecewise extension for p=floor(a/2)+1 through 2a, not the known first phase. Subwattanachai 2023 (arXiv:2309.09149) has divisibility prerequisites absent here. Exact semantic indexed searches reveal no statement implying the extension, but possible uncatalogued equivalent work remains.
residual_risks: Other indexed or unindexed literature could independently derive the same consecutive-triple formulas, including generic quasipolynomial inversion or large-s theories; noncoverage of all works cannot be proved.
Generalized Frobenius computations for a>120 or p>2a are not claimed.

value.rationale: Answers an explicit published open continuation for the simplest consecutive three-generator family over two full nontrivial parameter phases and an interval of levels growing linearly in a. A uniform new closed law exhibits two structural phase changes, permitting exact evaluation without Apéry tables for infinitely many (a,p); it is not a mere individual table lookup, renaming, or reproof of the known first regime.
